english: Consider the family of curves $y=\dfrac{c(x+1)}{x}$, $x\neq0$, where $c$ is a real parameter. The orthogonal trajectory of this family that passes through the point $(12,36)$ is part of a curve $\Gamma$ with a polynomial equation. The curve $\Gamma$ meets the $x$-axis at the origin and at exactly one more point $(\alpha,0)$. Then the value of $\alpha$ is ______.
hindi: वक्र-कुल $y=\dfrac{c(x+1)}{x}$, $x\neq0$ पर विचार कीजिए, जहाँ $c$ एक वास्तविक प्राचल है। इस कुल का बिन्दु $(12,36)$ से होकर जाने वाला लंबकोणीय संछेदी (orthogonal trajectory) एक वक्र $\Gamma$ का भाग है जिसका समीकरण बहुपदीय है। वक्र $\Gamma$, $x$-अक्ष से मूलबिन्दु पर तथा ठीक एक अन्य बिन्दु $(\alpha,0)$ पर मिलता है। तब $\alpha$ का मान ______ है।
solution_full: Differentiate $y=c\left(1+\dfrac1x\right)$: $y'=-\dfrac{c}{x^{2}}$. Eliminate $c=\dfrac{xy}{x+1}$: $y'=-\dfrac{y}{x(x+1)}$. This is the differential equation of the family.
For the orthogonal trajectories replace $y'$ by $-\dfrac{1}{y'}$: $y'=\dfrac{x(x+1)}{y}$.
Check of orthogonality at $(12,36)$: family slope $-\dfrac{36}{12\cdot13}=-\dfrac{3}{13}$, trajectory slope $\dfrac{12\cdot13}{36}=\dfrac{13}{3}$; product $-1$.
originality_note: New: the orthogonal trajectories of the hyperbolas y = c(x+1)/x are the cubic curves 3y^2 = 2x^3 + 3x^2 + const, and the one through (12,36) is the nodal cubic 3y^2 = x^2(2x + 3). Closest known: orthogonal trajectories of y = cx^n (ellipses). Different because: the family has a moving factor (x+1)/x, the trajectories are cubics, and the point makes the constant vanish. A first design (family x^2 + 3y^2 = cy) was found as a published exercise and was replaced.

concept_use.Orthogonal trajectories: The family's equation y' = -y/(x(x+1)) is formed, slopes are replaced by negative reciprocals, and the separable equation y dy = (x^2 + x) dx gives the trajectories 3y^2 = 2x^3 + 3x^2 + 6K.
